title: Let Language Constrain Geometry: Vision–Language Models as Semantic and Spatial Critics for 3D Generation
claim: A vision-language model critic scores renders of a 3D representation with a Yes/No log-odds signal, and its gradient updates generation.
layout: 1 wide panel, left-to-right flow, yellow prompt box at right, feedback arrow underneath
description: A single wide pipeline diagram read left to right. At far left is a neural-network icon labeled as different 3D generation paradigms: (1) optimization-based diffusion s_phi in blue and (2) feed-forward DiT sampler in purple, joined by an 'or' between dashed arrows. These point to a 3D representation theta, drawn as a hexagonal node lattice around a humanoid robot with a laptop. A camera icon leads to a 2x2 grid of rendered robot views, x_theta. A dashed arrow leads to a VLM robot icon. The text prompt box at top feeds into the VLM. A large yellow box at right holds the evaluation prompt, with criteria for content match and geometric quality and a strict Yes/No answer. A yellow feedback arrow runs along the bottom, back to the 3D representation. It is labeled 'VLM3D: Take Gradient on log p(YES) − log p(NO)'.
caption: Reproducing the "Embracing Peace" Statue with VLM3D. We challenge VLM3D's dual paradigms with San Diego's iconic monument. Top (Optimization-based): Given a long text description, baseline MVDream [ref] suffers a catastrophic semantic failure, omitting the nurse entirely. Our VLM3D critic successfully recovers both figures and their signature pose. Key details are highlighted in red. Bottom (Feed-forward model-based): Comparing to the statue's reference image, baseline Hunyuan3D [ref] generates a distorted, spatially incoherent mesh. Our VLM3D substantially corrects these spatial failures and produces a more geometrically plausible 3D asset.
abstract: Text-to-3D generation has advanced rapidly, yet state-of-the-art models, encompassing both optimization-based and feed-forward architectures, still face two fundamental limitations. First, they struggle with coarse semantic alignment, often failing to capture fine-grained prompt details. Second, they lack robust 3D spatial understanding, leading to geometric inconsistencies and catastrophic failures in part assembly and spatial relationships. To address these challenges, we propose VLM3D, a general framework that repurposes large vision-language models (VLMs) as powerful, differentiable semantic and spatial critics. Our core contribution is a dual-query critic signal derived from the VLM's Yes or No log-odds, which assesses both semantic fidelity and geometric coherence. We demonstrate the generality of this guidance signal across two distinct paradigms: (1) As a reward objective for optimization-based pipelines, VLM3D significantly outperforms existing methods on standard benchmarks. (2) As a test-time guidance module for feed-forward pipelines, it actively steers the iterative sampling process of SOTA native 3D models to correct severe spatial errors. VLM3D establishes a principled and generalizable path to inject the VLM's rich, language-grounded understanding of both semantics and space into diverse 3D generative pipelines.
